messages:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing intermittent GPU slot starvation in eu-west1 after the interconnect had a brief flap ~30m ago. Multiple training pods stuck Pending with kubelet saying network not ready. Any visibility?

tom: I just noticed a spike in Pending counts for nodepool-gpu-a. Some pods get scheduled then evicted a few seconds later.

sree: Looking at node logs, CNI reports repeated veth reset/attach failures and we see kubelet setting 'NetworkPluginDown' then marking pod as NotReady. Packet loss between hosts in the same AZ around that time.

sree: snippet from one kubelet: ```Mar 18 10:07:12 node-123 kubelet[1234]: NetworkPlugin cni failed, err: "failed to set up pod"
Mar 18 10:07:13 node-123 kubelet[1234]: Pod  kube-system/rt-training-abc marked NotReady: NetworkPluginDown```

deploy-bot: deploy/announcements: BGP mesh change rolled to eu-west1 at 10:02 UTC (id: bgp-roll-2026-03-18). If you suspect networking, ping networking-team.

alex: @networking are you seeing any interconnect drops? if the overlay between hosts is flapping, scheduler bounces will pile up -> apparent slot starvation. Could also be kube-proxy conntrack exhaustion.

lina: We don't want a long-term AZ-constricting fix, but short term can we stop cross-AZ packing for GPU pods? If scheduler avoids packing across AZs we won't lose slot utilization due to network ripples. Cost + utilization tradeoff though. :thinking_face: 

tom: suggestion: temporary nodeSelector/topology spread? But manual edits are painful. Better to toggle scheduler config to prefer zone-affinity for the GPU queue.

sree: I ran an iperf test between two GPU hosts in same AZ and saw 12% packet loss for a 90s window right when the incident started. I'm running a 5m probe across multiple pairs now and will post results.

alex: If we flip scheduler preference, we'll consolidate loads into fewer AZs which raises risk of AZ-wide outage but reduces eviction ripple. Need to quantify how many GPUs we lose currently vs extra idle capacity if we force packing.

maya: Agreed. Action plan: 1) sree to finish network probes + paste results (ETA 15m). 2) tom to prepare a scheduler policy tweak to prefer zone-local scheduling for label 'redwood/gpu=true' (dry-run in staging). 3) alex to ask infra/networking about rolling back bgp change if probes show underlying fabric issue. I'll open an incident page.

lina: Quick mitigation option: set a temporary PodSpec annotation to prefer nodes with topology.kubernetes.io/zone via mutating webhook for gpu pods. Low-risk and reversible.

sree: probe results: most pairs stable now, but two host pairs show persistent interconnect jitter. Uploading pcap to S3 -> s3://redwood-ops/pcaps/2101234567-iperf.pcap.

maya: Thanks. If networking confirms fabric instability we roll back bgp-roll. If it's limited to a handful of hosts we can cordon/drain and reprovision.

tom: I'll post scheduler policy diff in ~10m. If we do the preference change, let's add a short-lived flag in our config so we can revert automatically after 6h.

alex: Noted — I'll also model cost impact: if we consolidate GPUs into 1 AZ, expected 7% increase in per-request latency for multi-region customers and ~12% increase in burst cost due to less binpacking. I'll attach numbers to the incident.

maya: Cool. TL;DR: network blip caused pod network readiness failures -> scheduler churn -> apparent GPU slot starvation. Short-term: prefer zone-local scheduling for GPU label while infra investigates. Longer-term: improve host-level interconnect monitoring + safer binpacking heuristics. :white_check_mark:
